title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck stratifies the Mumford–Deligne compactification \hat M_{g,ν} (he writes 'MD'; today 'Deligne–Mumford') by combinatorial types of stable curves, i.e. by 'MD-graphs' G (the dual graph). A vertex α carries a genus g_α, and \hat I_α is the set of half-edges plus marked points at α, with \hat ν_α = card \hat I_α. Edges correspond to nodes. On the previous page he notes that each stratum M_[G] is a finite quotient of M_G ≅ ∏_α M_{g_α,\hat I_α}. That gives formula (27): dim M_G/Z = Σ_α (3(g_α−1)+\hat ν_α) = 3Σg_α − 3s_0 + ν + 2s_1. Here s_0 is the number of vertices and s_1 the number of edges. Each edge contributes two half-edges, so Σ\hat ν_α = ν + 2s_1.

On this page he converts this count using the Euler characteristic of the connected graph, s_0 − s_1 = 1 − h_1, where h_1 is the first Betti number. This gives −3s_0 + 2s_1 = −3(s_0 − s_1) − s_1 = 3(h_1 − 1) − s_1. Using the arithmetic-genus formula g = Σg_α + h_1, he gets (28): dim M_G/Z = [3(g−1)+ν] − s_1. The bracket is dim \hat M_{g,ν}/Z, i.e. 3g−3+ν. Hence (29): the codimension of the stratum M_[G] in \hat M_{g,ν} is s_1, the number of edges, i.e. the number of double points of curves of type G.

He then names two invariants:
- μ(G) = Σ_α (3(g_α−1)+\hat ν_α) = 3(g−1)+ν−s_1 is the 'modular dimension' of the MD-graph (formula (30)).
- s_1 = card A = card(Ã)/2 is the 'modular codimension'. It vanishes iff G is the trivial reduced graph: one vertex, no edges.

The next page notes that the open stratum (codimension 0) is the simplest, and the most complex strata are those of modular dimension 0, i.e. codimension 3g−3+ν. These are the maximally degenerate curves, built from 3-pointed P^1's (pants decompositions). This serves the larger programme of describing the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}: the boundary stratification, its specialization order, and the compactified strata \hat M_G = ∏ \hat M_{g_α,\hat I_α}.
errors: No mathematical errors. The computation −3s_0+2s_1 = 3(h_1−1)−s_1 uses s_0−s_1 = 1−h_1, which holds because the dual graph is connected; this is implicit.
'dim /Z' means relative dimension over Spec Z, not absolute dimension. This is consistent throughout.
Formula (30) requires each vertex to be stable (2g_α−2+\hat ν_α > 0); this is implicit in the MD-graph notion.
Minor imprecision: M_[G] is a finite quotient of M_G (by Aut G), not M_G itself, but the dimension is unaffected.
In (30) the summand should read \hat ν_α (half-edges plus marked points), not ν_α, for the second equality to hold. The image appears to have a hat or tilde there.

ideas.what: Stratification of \hat M_{g,ν} by dual graphs of stable curves, with stratum ≅ (∏_v M_{g_v,n_v})/Aut(G)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, correct rederivation of the standard fact that boundary strata of Deligne–Mumford spaces have codimension equal to the number of nodes. Only the terminology (modular dimension/codimension of an MD-graph) is Grothendieck-specific, and it already appears in spirit in Esquisse d'un programme.
transcription_corrections: Equation labels (28) and (29) appear overwritten in the image (originally (27)/(28)); the final labels are (28) and (29).
In (30) the summand appears to be \hat ν_α (hatted, possibly a tilde), not ν_α.
The last displayed line of the top computation reads '= −3+3h_1 − s_1 = 3(h_1−1)−s_1', with the final term partly cut off at the margin.
